files.content:
# Supply-chain gate referenced by deny.toml: cargo-deny (advisories, licenses,
# bans, sources) against the committed Cargo.lock, on every PR and on a weekly
# schedule so newly published RUSTSEC advisories are caught between releases.
name: Security / supply chain

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # weekly, Monday 06:00 UTC

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  cargo-deny:
    name: cargo-deny check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # deny.toml targets the modern (cargo-deny 0.16+ / action 2.x) schema.
      # --all-features forces the local-only crates (SQLCipher stack, age,
      # argon2, keyring, ...) into the dependency-graph traversal so both the
      # cloud and local/fleet surfaces are covered by one run.
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2
        with:
          arguments: --all-features
          command: check

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

# Cancel superseded runs on the same ref — a force-push shouldn't leave a stale red/green.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Fail on warnings in CI. The OSS fleet build is warning-clean; keep it that way.
  RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings
  # The OSS self-host fleet-worker feature set (see README "Feature flags"). This is the build
  # actual users run, so it is the one every job below exercises first.
  OSS_FEATURES: --no-default-features --features local,fleet,openai

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The build users actually run.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  fleet:
    name: Fleet worker (build + test)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install build dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config libssl-dev
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      # The Playwright driver is fetched by vendor/playwright-rs/build.rs and cached OUTSIDE
      # target/, so cache it explicitly — otherwise every cold run re-downloads ~45 MB.
      - name: Cache Playwright driver
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/playwright-rs-driver
          key: pw-driver-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('vendor/playwright-rs/build.rs') }}
      # `--locked` everywhere: a lockfile that does not match Cargo.toml is a CI failure, not a
      # silent update. Without it, drift is invisible until a release build behaves differently.
      - name: cargo build (release binary — the shippable artifact)
        run: cargo build --release --locked ${{ env.OSS_FEATURES }} --bin writ-agent-fleet
      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --locked ${{ env.OSS_FEATURES }}
      - name: cargo test (auto-update signature verification)
        run: cargo test --locked --features local,update-test-keys --test update_verify

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The DESKTOP configuration. `README.md` ships `writ-agentd` and `writ` as two of the four
  # binaries, and their documented build (`--no-default-features --features local,openai`) is a
  # THIRD feature combination that neither of the other jobs type-checks: it has the local engine
  # without `fleet` and without `cloud`, so cfg-gated code reachable only in that shape is otherwise
  # never compiled. A binary we document has to be a binary we build.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  desktop-build:
    name: Desktop daemon + CLI (local only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install build dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config libssl-dev
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Cache Playwright driver
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/playwright-rs-driver
          key: pw-driver-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('vendor/playwright-rs/build.rs') }}
      - name: cargo check (desktop feature set)
        run: cargo check --locked --no-default-features --features local,openai --all-targets
      - name: build both desktop binaries
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --features local,openai \
            --bin writ-agentd --bin writ
      - name: cargo test (desktop feature set)
        run: cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features local,openai --lib

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The build a visitor gets from a bare `cargo build`. It must also be clean —
  # this configuration was previously unchecked and carried 17 warnings.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  default-build:
    name: Default build (managed cloud)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install build dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config libssl-dev
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Cache Playwright driver
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/playwright-rs-driver
          key: pw-driver-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('vendor/playwright-rs/build.rs') }}
      - run: cargo check --locked --all-targets
      - name: cargo test (lib)
        run: cargo test --locked --lib

  # NOTE: there is deliberately NO `cargo fmt --check` gate. This tree predates any rustfmt config,
  # so `cargo fmt` rewrites ~14k lines — a gate that fails on day one, and a reformat that would bury
  # real changes in churn. `rustfmt.toml` pins the width the code was written at so editors behave;
  # clippy below is the gate that catches things that matter. Both feature configurations are
  # currently clippy-clean, so this is enforceable rather than aspirational.
  clippy:
    name: Clippy (both feature configurations)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install build dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config libssl-dev
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Cache Playwright driver
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/playwright-rs-driver
          key: pw-driver-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('vendor/playwright-rs/build.rs') }}
      - name: clippy (OSS fleet worker)
        run: cargo clippy --locked ${{ env.OSS_FEATURES }} --all-targets
      # The default/cloud configuration compiles a different half of the crate (saas_bridge, the
      # gateway, the cloud API) that the OSS feature set never type-checks. Lint it too.
      - name: clippy (default / managed cloud)
        run: cargo clippy --locked --all-targets

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Cross-platform: detect_platform() claims macOS and Windows support, so prove it.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  cross:
    name: Build (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [macos-latest, windows-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Cache Playwright driver
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/playwright-rs-driver
          key: pw-driver-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('vendor/playwright-rs/build.rs') }}
      - run: cargo check --locked ${{ env.OSS_FEATURES }}

  msrv:
    # NOT `${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}` — a job-level `name` can only see the github, needs,
    # strategy, matrix, vars and inputs contexts. Referencing `steps` there is a workflow-file
    # validation error that rejects the WHOLE file, so no job in it runs at all. The resolved
    # version is echoed by the "Read rust-version from Cargo.toml" step below instead.
    name: MSRV (rust-version from Cargo.toml)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install build dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config libssl-dev
      - name: Read rust-version from Cargo.toml
        id: msrv
        run: echo "version=$(grep -m1 '^rust-version' Cargo.toml | cut -d'"' -f2)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Cache Playwright driver
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/playwright-rs-driver
          key: pw-driver-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('vendor/playwright-rs/build.rs') }}
      # The declared MSRV must be real. If this fails, RAISE `rust-version` in Cargo.toml —
      # do not delete this job.
      - run: cargo check --locked ${{ env.OSS_FEATURES }}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The primary documented install path. It was never exercised, and was broken.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  docker:
    name: Docker image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: docker build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: false
          load: true
          tags: writ-agent:ci
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
      # Prove the binary actually starts in the runtime stage — this is what catches a
      # builder/runtime glibc mismatch, which a successful `docker build` alone does not.
      #
      # ASSERT ON THE OUTPUT, not just the exit code. The Dockerfile primes dependencies with stub
      # `fn main() {}` sources, and a cargo freshness misfire can leave those stubs as the shipped
      # binary — which starts, exits 0, prints nothing, and sails through an exit-code-only check.
      # This image did precisely that until it was caught. Grepping the real version string is what
      # makes the stub fail.
      - name: Smoke test the image
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          out=$(docker run --rm --entrypoint /app/writ-agent-fleet writ-agent:ci --version)
          echo "$out"
          echo "$out" | grep -qE '^writ-agent-fleet [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' \
            || { echo "::error::binary produced no version banner — is this the stub build?"; exit 1; }
          docker run --rm --entrypoint /app/writ-agent-fleet writ-agent:ci --help | grep -q 'WRIT_COORDINATOR_URL'

      # `--help` deliberately touches nothing, so it cannot see a missing browser driver. The
      # driver's compile-time path points into the BUILDER stage; if the copy into the runtime
      # stage is ever dropped, the image still builds, still starts, still reports healthy — and
      # fails every single run at browser launch. Assert the layout `find_sibling_driver` expects.
      - name: Both drivers survived into the runtime stage
        run: |
          docker run --rm --entrypoint sh writ-agent:ci -c '
            set -e
            # Vanilla driver — without it the first browser launch dies with ServerNotFound,
            # because the compile-time path points into the builder stage.
            test -x /app/playwright-driver/node
            test -f /app/playwright-driver/package/cli.js
            /app/playwright-driver/node --version

            # patchright STEALTH driver. Its absence is silent: `find_patchright_driver` simply
            # falls through to the vanilla one, logs a warning, and every run goes out with
            # Runtime.enable on — detectable, and slower. The image looked healthy in exactly
            # that state before it was staged here, so assert it rather than trust the build.
            test -x /app/patchright-driver/node
            test -f /app/patchright-driver/package/cli.js
            /app/patchright-driver/node --version
          '

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Attribution must never silently drift (AGPL §4/§5 obligation).
  #
  # ADVISORY HERE, ENFORCED AT PUBLISH. This job reports drift but does not block, because in a
  # cold CI environment it is NOT DETERMINISTIC: `cargo-about` reads each crate's license text out
  # of `registry/src/`, which only `cargo build` populates — `cargo fetch` leaves `.crate` archives
  # unextracted. For whichever crates happen to be missing, cargo-about silently falls back to the
  # generic SPDX text instead of the crate's own LICENSE file, and *which* crates those are moves
  # with whatever `rust-cache` restored. Two consecutive runs on near-identical trees produced two
  # entirely different diffs. A check that disagrees with itself cannot gate a merge.
  #
  # The real gate is `scripts/publish-agent.sh`, which runs the same comparison AFTER a full build,
  # so every crate's source is extracted and the output is stable. That is also the only moment the
  # attribution actually ships. Read a failure here as "look at the notices", not "the tree is bad".
  # To make this blocking again, build the whole dependency graph first — note `--all-features`
  # cannot be used for that, since `captcha_solver` and `ip_relay` have no source in this repo.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  notices:
    name: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES is current (advisory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      # PIN THE VERSION. Two separate traps here, both of which made this job unrunnable:
      #   1. `cargo-about` 0.9.x puts its binary behind a `cli` feature, so a plain
      #      `cargo install cargo-about` compiles the LIBRARY, installs no binary, and exits 0 with
      #      only a warning — the next step then dies on `no such command: about`.
      #   2. Different cargo-about versions render different output, so an unpinned installer turns
      #      this gate into a coin flip that fails on an unrelated day.
      # The pin must match whatever generated the committed THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. When you bump
      # it, regenerate the file in the same commit.
      - name: Install cargo-about
        run: cargo install cargo-about --locked --version 0.6.6
      # `cargo about generate --offline` runs `cargo metadata`, which resolves the WHOLE graph out
      # of the local registry cache — including optional deps like `age` that no default build
      # pulls. A developer's cache is warm so this is invisible locally; a fresh runner's is empty
      # and resolution fails with a misleading "no matching package named `age`". Populate the cache
      # from the lockfile first, which is also what keeps `--offline` meaningful: nothing outside
      # Cargo.lock can be reached afterwards.
      - name: Populate the registry cache from Cargo.lock
        run: cargo fetch --locked
      - name: Regenerate and diff
        run: |
          cargo about generate --offline --all-features about.hbs > /tmp/notices.md
          if ! diff -u THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md /tmp/notices.md; then
            echo "::error::THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is stale. Regenerate with:"
            echo "::error::  cargo about generate --offline --all-features about.hbs > THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"
            exit 1
          fi

name: Release

# Publishes what the README promises: fleet-worker binaries on the Releases page and
# ghcr.io/usewrit/writ-agent. Before this existed, both links were dead on arrival.
on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Tag to build (e.g. v1.0.0). Creates a draft release.'
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: write   # create the release + upload assets
  packages: write   # push to ghcr

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  OSS_FEATURES: --no-default-features --features local,fleet,openai

jobs:
  binaries:
    name: ${{ matrix.target }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { os: ubuntu-latest,  target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu,  name: writ-agent-fleet-linux-x86_64 }
          - { os: ubuntu-24.04-arm, target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, name: writ-agent-fleet-linux-aarch64 }
          - { os: macos-latest,   target: aarch64-apple-darwin,      name: writ-agent-fleet-macos-arm64 }
          # `macos-15-intel`, not `macos-13`: GitHub retired the macOS 13 image, and a job whose
          # runs-on label has no runners does not fail — it sits QUEUED (for hours, then a day),
          # holding up every job that needs it. That is what stalled the first v1.0.0 release with
          # four of five binaries already built. If this ever queues indefinitely again, the label
          # is the first thing to check.
          - { os: macos-15-intel, target: x86_64-apple-darwin,       name: writ-agent-fleet-macos-x86_64 }
          - { os: windows-latest, target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc,    name: writ-agent-fleet-windows-x86_64 }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref }}
      - name: Install build dependencies (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config libssl-dev
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Cache Playwright driver
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/playwright-rs-driver
          key: pw-driver-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('vendor/playwright-rs/build.rs') }}

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --release --locked ${{ env.OSS_FEATURES }} --bin writ-agent-fleet --target ${{ matrix.target }}

      # A BARE BINARY IS NOT A SHIPPABLE ARTIFACT HERE.
      #
      # `vendor/playwright-rs`'s build.rs bakes an absolute path to the Playwright driver into the
      # binary — this runner's `target/…/out` or `~/.cache/playwright-rs-driver/…`. Neither exists
      # on the machine that downloads the release, so a bare binary starts, connects to the
      # coordinator and reports healthy, then fails EVERY run at browser launch with
      # `ServerNotFound`. So ship the driver with it: the archive unpacks to a directory holding the
      # binary and a `playwright-driver/` beside it, which `browser::install::find_sibling_driver`
      # resolves with no configuration from the operator.
      - name: Stage artifact (+ SHA-256)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          stage="stage/${{ matrix.name }}"
          mkdir -p "$stage" dist

          src="target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/writ-agent-fleet"
          if [ -f "$src.exe" ]; then cp "$src.exe" "$stage/writ-agent-fleet.exe"; else cp "$src" "$stage/writ-agent-fleet"; fi

          # build.rs either extracts into this build's OUT_DIR or reuses the machine cache that the
          # `Cache Playwright driver` step above restores. Look in both; a miss is fatal, never a
          # silently driver-less archive.
          cli_js="$(find "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/build" "$HOME/.cache/playwright-rs-driver" \
                        -type f -path '*/package/cli.js' 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
          if [ -z "$cli_js" ]; then echo "FATAL: no Playwright driver produced by build.rs" >&2; exit 1; fi
          driver_dir="$(dirname "$(dirname "$cli_js")")"
          cp -R "$driver_dir" "$stage/playwright-driver"
          # `node` must survive as an executable or the archive is useless.
          if [ ! -f "$stage/playwright-driver/node.exe" ]; then chmod +x "$stage/playwright-driver/node"; fi

          if [ "${{ runner.os }}" = "Windows" ]; then
            asset="${{ matrix.name }}.zip"
            (cd stage && 7z a -tzip "../dist/$asset" "${{ matrix.name }}" >/dev/null)
          else
            asset="${{ matrix.name }}.tar.gz"
            tar -C stage -czf "dist/$asset" "${{ matrix.name }}"
          fi

          # Publish a checksum next to every archive so operators can verify what they downloaded.
          cd dist
          if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null; then
            sha256sum "$asset" > "$asset.sha256"
          else
            shasum -a 256 "$asset" > "$asset.sha256"
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.name }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error

  # BUILD EACH ARCH ON ITS OWN NATIVE RUNNER, then stitch a manifest.
  #
  # This used to be one job doing `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64` behind `setup-qemu-action`,
  # which means arm64 was EMULATED: a full Rust release build plus a Chromium install running under
  # QEMU on an amd64 host. It ran for over an hour and a half without finishing and blocked the whole
  # release. `ubuntu-24.04-arm` is already used by the binaries matrix above and finishes in minutes,
  # so there is no reason to emulate anything. Each arch pushes by digest, and the manifest job below
  # joins the digests under the real tags.
  image:
    name: ghcr image (${{ matrix.arch }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { arch: amd64, platform: linux/amd64, runner: ubuntu-latest }
          - { arch: arm64, platform: linux/arm64, runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref }}
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
          # push-by-digest: no tag is claimed here — the manifest job owns the tags, so a half-built
          # matrix can never leave `latest` pointing at a single-arch image.
          outputs: type=image,name=ghcr.io/usewrit/writ-agent,push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true
          # Scope the cache per arch; a shared scope makes the two jobs evict each other.
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=img-${{ matrix.arch }}
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=img-${{ matrix.arch }}
      - name: Export digest
        run: |
          mkdir -p /tmp/digests
          echo "${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}" > "/tmp/digests/${{ matrix.arch }}"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: image-digest-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: /tmp/digests/*
          if-no-files-found: error

  image-manifest:
    name: ghcr manifest
    needs: [image]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: /tmp/digests
          pattern: image-digest-*
          merge-multiple: true
      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/usewrit/writ-agent
          # Derive every tag from the SAME ref the checkout used. Without the explicit `value=`,
          # `type=semver` reads `github.ref`, which on a `workflow_dispatch` is the BRANCH — so a
          # manual run produced no version tags at all and (via `is_default_branch`) pushed a bare
          # `latest` pointing at an untagged build, while the GitHub release beside it was still a
          # recoverable draft. `latest=false` turns off the implicit flavor so the one rule below
          # is the only thing that can publish `latest`, and it skips prereleases (`v1.1.0-rc.1`).
          flavor: latest=false
          tags: |
            type=semver,pattern={{version}},value=${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}},value=${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ !contains(inputs.tag || github.ref_name, '-') }}
      - name: Create and push the multi-arch manifest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          digests=""
          for f in /tmp/digests/*; do
            digests="$digests ghcr.io/usewrit/writ-agent@$(cat "$f")"
          done
          echo "joining:$digests"
          # shellcheck disable=SC2046
          docker buildx imagetools create \
            $(jq -cr '.tags | map("-t " + .) | join(" ")' <<< "$DOCKER_METADATA_OUTPUT_JSON") \
            $digests
      - name: Verify the manifest carries both architectures
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ref="ghcr.io/usewrit/writ-agent:$(jq -r '.tags[0] | split(":")[1]' <<< "$DOCKER_METADATA_OUTPUT_JSON")"
          docker buildx imagetools inspect "$ref" --format '{{json .Manifest}}' \
            | jq -e '[.manifests[].platform | select(.os=="linux") | .architecture] | (index("amd64") and index("arm64"))' \
            || { echo "::error::published manifest is missing an architecture"; exit 1; }

  release:
    name: GitHub Release
    needs: [binaries, image-manifest]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref }}
      # FILTER. Without `pattern` this downloads EVERY artifact in the run, which is no longer just
      # the release archives: the per-arch image jobs upload `image-digest-*`, and
      # `docker/build-push-action` uploads a `*.dockerbuild` build record of its own. Pulling all
      # nine (~290 MB) is how this job died on a blob-download retry — and had it succeeded,
      # `files: dist/*` below would have published the digest files and build records as release
      # assets. Only the archives and their checksums belong on the release page.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist
          pattern: writ-agent-fleet-*
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Show what will be attached
        run: ls -lh dist/
      - name: Create release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
          # A manual dispatch produces a DRAFT so a mis-tag is recoverable; a real tag push publishes.
          draft: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
          generate_release_notes: true
          files: dist/*
          body: |
            Self-host fleet worker for `writ-agent-fleet`.

            Each archive unpacks to a directory containing the binary and the Playwright driver it
            needs (`playwright-driver/`) — keep them together, the worker finds the driver beside
            itself. Chromium installs itself on first browser use.

            ```sh
            tar -xzf writ-agent-fleet-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
            cd writ-agent-fleet-linux-x86_64
            WRIT_SERVICE_TOKEN=… WRIT_COORDINATOR_URL=https://… ./writ-agent-fleet
            ```

            Verify a download against its `.sha256` before running it. Container image:
            `ghcr.io/usewrit/writ-agent:${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}`.

            See [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) for what changed, and the
            [coordinator](https://github.com/usewrit/writ) for the control plane this connects to.

-- Marketplace installs (consumer-owned, local-first protected executor).
--
-- One row per installed marketplace listing. The `sealed_recipe` column holds the listing's FROZEN
-- recipe snapshot, encrypted with THIS agent's per-agent Fernet channel key (the cloud seals it for
-- us at `/api/marketplace/installs/{slug}/sealed-recipe`). The PLAINTEXT recipe is NEVER stored: the
-- executor decrypts the sealed blob IN MEMORY at run time and discards it. The blob is additionally
-- protected at rest by the SQLCipher-encrypted DB (Layer A) and may be vault-field-wrapped (Layer B)
-- before storage. We persist listing METADATA (title/creator/price/free flag/input schema) for the
-- UI, but NEVER the steps.
--
-- Conventions match 0001/0002/0003: timestamps TEXT RFC3339 UTC; JSON fields TEXT; booleans INTEGER
-- 0/1; additive only.
CREATE TABLE installed_workflows (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,              -- marketplace listing slug (natural key)
    listing_title TEXT,                     -- display title (metadata only)
    creator TEXT,                           -- creator display name/handle (metadata only)
    is_free INTEGER NOT NULL,               -- 1 = free listing (run locally, no charge) | 0 = paid (metered)
    price_micros INTEGER,                   -- creator price-per-run in micro-USD (paid listings; reflection only)
    proxy_cloud_id TEXT,                    -- cloud proxy workflow id created by the install endpoint
    sealed_recipe TEXT NOT NULL,            -- channel_key-Fernet-sealed (then optionally vault-sealed) recipe blob
    input_schema TEXT,                      -- JSON: BYO input/secret slots the consumer must attach
    installed_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now')),
    last_run_at TEXT                        -- RFC3339 UTC of the most recent local run (NULL until first run)
);

-- Inline "setup steps" manifest for a monitor target: the recorded steps
-- (navigate/login/click) replayed in the browser BEFORE the content read, so a
-- check can run behind a login or after navigation. Stored as the JSON the shared
-- checker's `pre_check_workflow` hook expects: { "steps": [...], "credentials": {...} }.
-- NULL/absent = a plain check with no setup (the fast HTTP path stays unchanged).
ALTER TABLE targets ADD COLUMN setup_steps TEXT;
